facts_known: Complaint received 16 Nov 2026 by WhatsApp from the owner of A-11-02, Block A (occupied, owner, 10 share units).
Resident reports her mother was turned away at the guardhouse on Sunday 15 Nov 2026, about 8.30 p.m., because she did not want to hand over her IC.
The mother's IC number is recorded by the officer as ******-**-6634 (last four digits only).
Resident asks whether the guard is allowed to ask for the IC.
No reported source unit. The complaint concerns a guard's request, not a breach by a resident.
facts_missing: Mother's full name and whether she was pre-registered as a visitor (HR-4(4)).
Parcel the mother was visiting (HR-4(1) requires this to be registered).
Exactly what the guard asked for: showing an identification document, or handing it over.
Whether the guard recorded her name, parcel and last four digits, and whether the guard called the resident of the parcel visited (HR-4(3)).
Whether the mother is a proprietor or occupier, which affects BL-17(2).

rules.quote: The management corporation may require any person on the common property to identify himself for security purposes.
rules.applies: Gives the management corporation power to require identification of visitors on common property, including the guardhouse. This is the governing text. It does not say the IC must be handed over.

rules.quote: showing an identification document as required under by-law 17 of the Third Schedule.
rules.applies: House rule 4 requires visitors to show an identification document at the guardhouse. Under HR-4(2) the guard records only the last four digits and the document is returned at once and not kept. Under HR-4(3) a visitor who declines to identify may be refused entry, and the guard must call the resident. The guard's request is therefore allowed in principle. Whether the guard went beyond showing the document is still to be checked.

next_steps.action: Acknowledge the WhatsApp complaint by 17 Nov 2026 (one working day), using the acknowledge template, on the same WhatsApp channel.

Ask the resident for the missing facts: mother's name, parcel visited, whether pre-registered, what the guard asked for, and whether the guard called the resident. Do not act against the guard or any resident until these are in.

Ask the guard on duty for the 15 Nov 2026 guardhouse visitor register entry for about 8.30 p.m. (name, parcel, last four digits, time) and record what is seen, with date and time. Check that the guard followed HR-4(2) and HR-4(3).
Send the reply below once the acknowledgement is sent. Explain the rule by name and number and ask for the missing facts. Make no promise about the outcome.
No written notice to any parcel. No breach has been verified and none is alleged.

Reported as happening on 'yesterday', which is Sunday 15 November 2026. Damage seen on Sunday 15 November (officer record).

Resident asks who pays for the repair. The complaint is received 16 November 2026 at the walk-in counter.
facts_missing: Time the damage happened and time first seen, and whether any renovation work was taking place at A-17-05 on 15 November (Sunday).
Name of the contractor and the works being done (drilling, hacking, moving materials).
Photographs of the damage, from the resident if available.
Whether the protective padding was installed in the service lift before materials were moved, and whether the service lift was used.

rules.quote: Damage to the common property, including the lifts, caused by the renovation works shall be assessed by the management office. The cost of making good the damage shall be deducted from the renovation deposit, and any cost above the deposit is recoverable from the proprietor under by-law 27(7) of the Third Schedule.
rules.applies: Governs who bears the cost. Damage to the service lift from renovation works is assessed by the office and paid from the renovation deposit first; any excess is recoverable from the proprietor (the owner of A-17-05). This applies only once the damage and its cause are verified. It does not yet establish that A-17-05's works caused the damage.

rules.quote: A proprietor shall take full responsibility for any defect or damage to the common property as a result of the renovation works or repair works to his parcel and if any damages is caused the proprietor shall immediately at his own cost, rectify and make good the damage to the satisfaction of the management corporation.
rules.applies: The proprietor of the renovated unit is responsible for making good damage to common property caused by its renovation works, as cited under ABL-5(3). Applies only if the damage is verified as caused by those works.

rules.quote: Renovation works approved under by-law 27 of the Third Schedule may be carried out only between 9.00 a.m. and 5.30 p.m. from Monday to Friday, and between 9.00 a.m. and 1.00 p.m. on Saturday. No renovation works are permitted on Sundays or public holidays.
rules.applies: The damage was seen on Sunday 15 November. If on-site or other facts show works were carried out that day, that would need to be verified against this rule. Do not assume it from the damage date alone. No conflict with BL-27 on this point.

next_steps.action: Acknowledge the complaint today (16 Nov 2026) at the walk-in counter, by the same channel the resident used.

Record the facts above. Ask the resident for the time of the damage, photographs, the contractor's name, and what they saw of works on 15 November. Do not contact or act against A-17-05 on the resident's report alone.

Have the guard or a staff member check the service lift door on site, record what is seen with date and time, and check the renovation record for A-17-05: approved works, deposit status (ABL-5(1)), padding (ABL-5(2)), and works hours for 15 November (ABL-4).
Log the lift door damage as a maintenance work order for the common property and give the resident the reference number.
Assess the cost under ABL-5(3) and BL-27(7) once the damage is verified and linked to A-17-05's works. Use the deposit first; the balance is recoverable from the proprietor.

Only after the breach is verified, the office may send a written notice to the proprietor of A-17-05, citing ABL-5(3) and BL-27(7) and the step required. Do not send a notice on the unverified report.
